Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

happen verb

take place

also occur, take place, come about, happen to someone, it happened that, happen to (befall)

classical

Cic. Fam. 14.8.1: sī quid acciderit novī
Caes. BG 4.29.1: accidit ut esset lūna plēna
Traupman 325

1accidī: short i in the perfect (Lewis & Short ac-cĭdo, cīdi, the perfect of ac-cīdo, cut down). A compound of cadō, cecidī; Lewis & Short marks the perfect short in the other compounds: dē-cĭdo, cĭdi; incĭdo, cĭdi; occĭdo, cĭdi.

accidō1, accidere, accidī

verb, third conjugation; impersonal accidit, with the dative of the person and ut with the subjunctive

happen, occur; befall

Of what happens unexpectedly, and above all of what goes wrong: sī quid adversī acciderit (Cic. Ac. 2.121, Lewis & Short). What happens is the subject, or an ut-clause; the person it happens to goes in the dative: quid tibi accidit?.

Other words

  • fīō, fierī, factus sum — happen, come about

    verb, irregular: the passive of faciō, conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.11.2: ecquid fit?; Traupman 100: quid factum est?; Traupman 109: fīō, take place; Traupman 325

    The everyday word: quid fit?, what’s going on?; ut fit, as usually happens; fit ut, it comes about that (see what happened?).

  • ēveniō, ēvenīre, ēvēnī, ēventum — happen, turn out

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 24.13: hoc nōbīs quoque majusculīs puerīs ēvenit; Ter. Ph. 65–66: ēvēnit senibus ambōbus simul iter … ut esset; Traupman 294

    Of things good or bad, especially as they turn out in the end.

  • contingō, contingere, contigī, contāctum — happen (to someone), usually of good luck

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Gell. 9.3.5: quod nāscī contigit temporibus vītae tuae; Quint. 1.1.7: quibus discere ipsīs nōn contigit; Traupman 325

    With the dative and an infinitive or ut: what someone has the luck to do.

  • incidō, incidere, incidī — occur, take place, fall out

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 353

  • obveniō, obvenīre, obvēnī, obventum — come up, fall to one’s lot

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 353

Examples

  • Item posthāc, sī quid opus erit, sī quid acciderit novī, faciēs ut sciam.

    And in future too, if anything is needed, if anything new happens, let me know.Cic. Fam. 14.8.1

  • Eādem nocte accidit ut esset lūna plēna

    That same night it happened that there was a full moonCaes. BG 4.29.1

  • sed heus tū! quid agis? ecquid fit?

    but hey, you! How are you? Anything happening?Cic. Fam. 7.11.2

  • fēcit statim, ut fit, fastīdium cōpia

    plenty, as usually happens, soon bred boredomLiv. 3.1.7

See also event, what happened?, tell me what happened, happen, result.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 100, 109, 294, 325.
